record.paper_title: Open questions in quarkonium and electromagnetic probes
record.original_question: What is the correct open-charm production baseline for interpreting intermediate-mass dimuon measurements, given that direct charm cross-section measurements imply a value about two times smaller than the charm yield needed to describe the proton-nucleus dimuon data collected by NA50?

evidence.quote: Also the understanding of the open charm baseline is under question, given that the charm production cross section deduced from the measurements made by many experiments (Fig. 11-left) is two times smaller than the value required to describe the dimuon data collected by NA50 in p-A collisions (Fig. 11-right).
This indicates that there seems to be something "anomalous" already in the intermediate mass dimuons produced in the p-A collisions studied by NA50.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider proton–nucleus (p–A) collisions at CERN-SPS fixed-target energies (proton beam momentum of order 400–450 GeV/c) and the production of muon pairs (dimuons) in the intermediate-mass region (roughly 1.5 GeV/c² < M_{μμ} < 2.5 GeV/c², between the φ and the J/ψ resonances). The dimuon mass and transverse-momentum spectra in this region are conventionally described as a superposition of two "expected" sources: (i) the Drell–Yan process, and (ii) correlated semileptonic decays of open-charm pairs (D D̄ → μ⁺μ⁻ + X), normalized by an open-charm production cross section σ_{cc̄}.

Direct measurements of charm production (from D-meson and single-lepton observables across multiple experiments) yield a value of σ_{cc̄}(p–A) that is approximately a factor of two smaller than the open-charm yield needed to reproduce the intermediate-mass dimuon spectra measured in p–A collisions when only Drell–Yan and open-charm semileptonic decays are included as sources.

Problem: Determine the correct open-charm baseline for the interpretation of intermediate-mass dimuon spectra in p–A collisions. Equivalently, identify and quantify the physical mechanism(s) responsible for the discrepancy between (a) the open-charm cross section σ_{cc̄} inferred from direct charm measurements and (b) the effective open-charm normalization required to describe the intermediate-mass dimuon data, and decide whether the excess in the intermediate-mass dimuon yield in p–A collisions is due to enhanced open-charm production or to an additional prompt dimuon source (such as thermal/partonic radiation or other non-charm contributions).
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent measurements by NA60 using a vertex pixel tracker separated prompt dimuons from open-charm decay dimuons in the intermediate-mass region. The data showed that the intermediate-mass excess is predominantly of prompt origin rather than from enhanced open-charm production, with open-charm yields consistent with direct charm measurements within uncertainties. The prompt excess is widely interpreted as thermal radiation from a partonic source. While this resolves the qualitative picture (the excess is not anomalous open-charm enhancement), a fully quantitative theoretical description of the p–A intermediate-mass dimuon baseline remains an active topic, so the question is best characterized as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Quantifying the Prompt Intermediate Mass Dimuon Excess in In-In Collisions Measured by NA60
status_evidence.snippet: NA60 separates prompt dimuons from open-charm decay dimuons using a pixel vertex tracker and shows that the intermediate-mass excess is of prompt origin.
status_evidence.claim: The intermediate-mass dimuon excess attributed earlier to anomalous open charm is shown by NA60 to be prompt, not from enhanced charm decays.

status_evidence.title: A first look at open charm production in Indium-Indium collisions at SPS energies
status_evidence.snippet: Open charm yields measured directly in In-In collisions are consistent with expectations from direct charm measurements, not with the larger normalization needed to fit the IMR dimuon spectrum assuming only Drell-Yan + open charm.
status_evidence.claim: Direct measurements of charm in heavy-ion collisions favor the smaller σ_{cc̄} value, implying the IMR excess requires an additional prompt source.
